narration: Welcome to the Harappan Civilization gallery. Here we have the Unicorn Seal, accession number NM 52.9/4, a small but striking steatite stamp measuring just over three centimeters square. It depicts a one‑horned animal—an image that appears on more Harappan seals than any other motif—facing a ritual stand, with a brief Indus script line above. Though we still do not know what the “unicorn” symbol meant, its frequent use suggests it held special significance in the daily or ceremonial life of the Indus Valley people. This seal was unearthed at Mohenjo‑daro by the Archaeological Survey of India and became part of the National Museum’s founding Harappan collection in 1949.
